SynthMaven development source | Introduction5

INTRODUCTION

SynthMaven 4: the oriental groove box

OPEN THIS SCREENThis page explains what SynthMaven 4 is for.
What it is
An FM-1 firmware for oriental live musicians, turning the standard M-VAVE FM-1 into an oriental groove box.
At a glance
14 sound engines, 610 melodic presets, 4 drum kits, 70 scales (46 of them maqam), 4 simultaneous layers plus the drummer, and 8 factory drum grooves.
Microtuning for maqam
46 maqam settings, a selectable root and octave boundary, custom offsets per key (10-cent steps on the panel, 1-cent steps in the editors), per-part bypass and scale-aware chords.
Multi-layer key mapping
Four parts per program, stacked or split across the keyboard, each with its own range, level and pan.
Groove box
An independent eight-lane drum machine beside all four parts, with factory grooves including Maksoom, Wahda, Baladi and Fox.
Sequencer
Up to 64 steps and 8 patterns per track, song arrangement, live recording, step chance, knob automation and a piano roll.
Song arranger
Up to 16 sections, each with a pattern for every track, a drum groove and 1-16 repeats, on the FM-1 or in the editors. A jam can become an arrangement.
MainStage-style performance
Programs with four scenes, a 32-entry setlist and learned pedal or controller actions, with a Perform screen in the web editor and the SM FM1 iPad app.
Multi-keyboard support
A separate MIDI input and channel for each layer and the drummer, over USB, TRS or both.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Install SynthMaven and start on Program 1.
  2. Tap SEL to choose a maqam.
  3. Press HOME to reach the drums, choose a groove with ALGORITHM and press PLAY.
  4. Play over it, then hold GLO for two seconds to bring in the other layers.

INTRODUCTION

The design: cards, knobs and themes

OPEN THIS SCREENHold HOME for Settings, then choose COLOR.
Cards
Every page shows its four knobs as cards along the top, in the same order as KNOB 1-4. Each card has its colour along the top, its label and its value.
Colours
KNOB 1-4 and layers 1-4 use the theme's four colours in order, on every screen.
SYNTHMAVEN
The default: red as the main colour, then white, blue and grey.
ORANGE
Orange as the main colour, then white, blue and grey.
BABY BLUE
Baby blue as the main colour, then white, red and grey.
PINK
Pink as the main colour, then white, blue and grey.
Type
All screens use Rubik, with a smaller size on the Home cards so that names fit. The pixel font is gone.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Hold HOME to open Settings.
  2. With COLOR selected, turn KNOB 1 to change the theme; it applies straight away.
  3. Turn KNOB 4 to leave.

FIRST 10 MINUTES

First 10 minutes

OPEN THIS SCREENStart here after installing.
1. Choose a maqam
Tap SEL. Turn SELECT to choose a scale, KNOB 3 to choose the root and KNOB 4 to turn master tuning on.
2. Start a groove
Press HOME to reach the drums. Turn ALGORITHM to MAKSOOM or another groove, then press PLAY. Turn SELECT to set the tempo and KNOB 4 to set the drummer volume.
3. Bring in layers
Press HOME to return to the four cards. Hold GLO for two seconds to play all four layers together.
4. Choose a sound
Turn SELECT, once the drums are stopped, to choose a layer, then ALGORITHM for its engine and PRESETS for its sound.
5. Save your program
Stop playback and press SAVE to open PROGRAM. Turn KNOB 4 right twice within 1.5 seconds to save.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Follow these in order the first time.
  2. Back up before you install, because installing resets settings and musical storage.

GETTING STARTED

Settings menu: hold HOME

OPEN THIS SCREENHold HOME.
SELECT
Move through the rows; it wraps from the last row to the first.
KNOB 1
Change the selected row.
KNOB 4
Leave the menu. KNOB 2 no longer moves the row.
MIDI MODE
Where the MIDI-only tracks accept notes: USB, TRS or BOTH. The default is BOTH.
USB ROLE
COMPUTER for the editors and the installer; HOST for a keyboard, pad or pedal connected to the FM-1. It returns to COMPUTER at each power-on.
MIDI KNOBS
Lets a MIDI controller work the panel. OFF: its knobs only send MIDI. ABSOLUTE: for knobs with fixed end stops. RELATIVE: for endless encoders.
HOLD and LIGHTS
Now in GLO preference pages, not this menu.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Hold HOME until Settings opens.
  2. Turn SELECT to the row.
  3. Turn KNOB 1 to change it.
  4. Turn KNOB 4 to leave.

GETTING STARTED

Scale list on Master Tune

OPEN THIS SCREENTap SEL.
SELECT or KNOB 1
Turn to open the list of full scale names over the keyboard. The tuning changes as you browse.
Stop turning
The list closes by itself and the keyboard shows the chosen scale.
OCT-
Close the list and put back the scale you started on.
Picker Popups off
The knob changes the scale directly, with no list.
Where a scale applies
Master Tune covers the layers ticked for it, from the chosen octave upward. Notes below that octave stay in equal temperament. Each layer also has its own scale on SCL, used when Master Tune is off.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Tap SEL.
  2. Turn SELECT through the list and listen.
  3. Stop turning to keep the scale.
SynthMaven development source | Getting started12

GETTING STARTED

Start here: controls and storage

Sound preset
One instrument sound. Factory sounds are read-only starting points; USER slots store individual edited sounds.
Program
Four parts with levels, pan, splits and scenes. P1-P8 are separate from the 384 USER sound slots.
Project
A-D stores the wider working setup, patterns and arrangement. Save a project after arranging a song.
Editor library
A named collection on your browser or iPad; it is not automatically a device save.
Master level
The physical MASTER knob controls listening level. Start low and raise gradually. Four layers share one processing budget; they do not each have a separate eight-voice allocation.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Connect power and let HOME appear. Choose a program, then play at a comfortable level.
  2. Select one part before editing its engine or sound. Save the complete program after mixing.
  3. Export a full backup before updating: a firmware flash restores factory settings and programs.
SynthMaven development source | Getting started13

GETTING STARTED

Install, back up and recover

Installer
Use the SynthMaven installer in a browser supporting Web MIDI/SysEx. Allow MIDI permission and select the FM-1.
Backup
Use Projects & backup > Save backup. Keep the downloaded archive outside browser storage.
Install
Select the current firmware and follow the installer prompts. Keep USB power connected throughout writing and verification.
Recovery
If the normal editor cannot connect, reopen the installer and follow its detected recovery/loader instructions. Use the release recovery package if required; never interrupt a write.
After update
Allow the device to restart, reconnect the editor and verify its version. Restore a backup only if you want its previous settings/programs.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Download the guide and release files first. Back up the working device.
  2. Run the installer through its final verification and restart.
  3. If a restart stalls after writing has completed, power-cycle and reconnect; do not power-cycle while writing.
SynthMaven development source | Getting started14

GETTING STARTED

USB computer, iPad and powered-host setup

COMPUTER role
Use GLO > USB / SAVE > ROLE = COMPUTER for the web editor or iPad. The computer/iPad is the USB host.
HOST role
Use HOST for a class-compliant USB MIDI keyboard, pad controller or pedal connected to the FM-1. This changes the FM-1 to host role. There is no separate keys-only or pedal-only USB mode.
Power and hub
The FM-1 cannot power the USB port, so a bus-powered controller needs a powered hub or powered OTG adapter. Connect the hub upstream cable to the FM-1, the controller to a USB-A data port and the charger to the hub power input. Hubs with two internal hub chips are supported. A slow hub can take up to about 3 seconds to be found.
TRS together
TRS MIDI IN stays active in either role. With GLO > MIDI/CPU > ROUT = PARTS, MIDI channels 1-4 play layers 1-4, so a USB controller and a TRS controller on different channels can play different layers.
Return to editor
One USB port cannot act as device and host simultaneously. Return to COMPUTER, reconnect the computer/iPad cable and choose the FM-1 MIDI ports.
iPad
Open SM FM1 in landscape and choose Connect > USB cable. USB Audio defaults to IN+OUT. iPadOS may cache the FM-1 name as SoundMaven; the corrected app also checks its USB identity and selects matching input/output automatically. Bluetooth is excluded.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Start in COMPUTER and confirm a normal editor connection.
  2. Disconnect the editor, choose HOST, connect the powered hub with the controller, wait up to 3 seconds and verify received MIDI.
  3. To edit again, return to COMPUTER before reconnecting the iPad or computer.
SynthMaven development source | Getting started15

GETTING STARTED

HOME: four-part program

OPEN THIS SCREENPress HOME.
SELECT
Choose the focused part, 1-4. While the drums are running it sets the tempo instead.
KNOB 4 with the drums running
Sets the drummer volume on both Home screens. Stop the drums and it goes back to its usual job.
ALGORITHM
Cycle engines for that part.
PRESET
Cycle sounds within the selected engine.
OCT- / OCT+
A short press transposes the keyboard. With layering on, it moves only the selected layer an octave (both together put it back), so each layer can sit in its own octave. On HOME, hold OCT- for three seconds for Program Down; hold OCT+ for Program Up.
EDIT / GLO holds
Hold EDIT two seconds for the persistent four-volume mixer. Hold GLO two seconds to toggle layering and display Layered ON/OFF.
Cards
Each part has a card: its role, sound, engine, pattern and steps. The selected card is outlined, and a dimmed card isn't sounding.
Rotary knobs
The four knobs under the cards show KNOB 1-4 for the selected part. Turn one to edit it.
HOME
Press HOME again to switch to the independent drum screen. Ordinary page controls are documented on their own pages.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Choose a program. Focus a part with SELECT.
  2. Choose its engine and preset; keep the other three parts as support.
  3. Hold EDIT to balance the four volumes, then SAVE the program.
SynthMaven development source | Getting started16

GETTING STARTED

Shortcuts and secondary actions

EDIT: two seconds
Open the mixer; release the button and continue mixing.
GLO: two seconds
Toggle layering, with a temporary Layered ON/OFF notification.
ENV: three seconds
Open the chord screen. Normal short ENV presses open envelopes.
SEL: three seconds
Open custom microtuning; a short press opens master tuning.
OCT buttons: three seconds
On HOME only, previous/next program. Short taps retain octave behavior.
SEQ hold
Open pattern selection; the normal hold threshold is about 0.7 seconds.
HOME hold
Open system/settings. FX hold is a separate configurable performance overlay; its threshold is set in GLO.
Confirm / cancel
OCT+ confirms an offered action; OCT- cancels/backs out. PROGRAM uses its own two-turn save/load confirmation.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Use a short press for the normal family page.
  2. For a special screen, hold until it opens, then release.
  3. Use HOME to return; navigating alone does not create a named save.
SynthMaven development source | Getting started17

Groove box

SynthMaven development source Illustrated Guide

SynthMaven development source | Groove box18

GROOVE BOX

Drum Home and factory grooves

OPEN THIS SCREENPress HOME on the four-part overview.
Editors
Studio > Drums has the same Groove control, plus Save pattern.
ALGORITHM
Choose a groove: BALLAD, HALF PIPE, STRAIGHT 8, ON THE FLOOR, MAKSOOM, WAHDA, BALADI or FOX. It replaces the eight lanes straight away.
MY PATTERN
Turn back to MY PATTERN to get your own steps again. Editing a groove makes it your pattern.
SELECT
Choose one of the eight lanes: KICK, SNARE, HAT, OPEN, CLAP, TOM, BELL or RIM. While the drums are running, SELECT sets the tempo instead, on both Home screens.
PRESETS / KNOB 1
Choose a step.
KNOB 2
Turn right to add a hit on the step, left to clear it.
KNOB 3 / KNOB 4
Set the lane level / set the tempo.
PLAY
Start or stop the independent drums. All four sound layers stay available to the keyboard.
Arabic rhythms
On these grooves dum plays KICK and TOM together, and tak plays RIM, SNARE and HAT together: MAKSOOM D T . T D . T . / BALADI D D . T D . T . / WAHDA D . . T . . T . / FOX D T D T.
Limits
The drum machine has 16 steps at 1/16 and no swing. Drum patterns save with the program.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Press HOME until DRUMS shows in the header.
  2. Turn ALGORITHM to the groove you want and press PLAY.
  3. Change the tempo with KNOB 4.
  4. Save the program to keep the drum pattern.

SEQUENCER

Recording a take

OPEN THIS SCREENSelect a track, then tap REC.
REC
Tap to arm or disarm the selected track. Only one track can be armed at a time.
REC + PLAY
Arm and start together.
Armed before PLAY
Records from step zero.
Armed while playing
Records from that track's next pattern start.
What is kept
Timing, velocity and held length, including repeats and overlapping chords.
Undo
After a take, hold EDIT for UNDO RECORDING. There is one such undo.
Click
Set click, click level and count-in in GLO > RECORDING. Set quantize on SEQ > TEMPO.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Select the track and an empty pattern.
  2. Set the click and count-in.
  3. Press REC + PLAY and perform.
  4. Stop, check NOTES, and save the project.
SynthMaven development source | Sequencer21

SEQUENCER

Song arranger on the FM-1

OPEN THIS SCREENPress SEQ and turn SELECT to SONG.
SEQ > SONG
The arranger: sections as columns and five rows, one per layer plus the drums.
KNOB 1
Choose the section.
KNOB 2
Choose the row: a layer, or the drums row below the last layer.
KNOB 3
Choose that layer's pattern in this section. On the drums row, choose the groove: same as before, a factory groove, MY PATTERN or off.
KNOB 4
Set how many times the section repeats, 1-16.
Limits
Up to 16 sections. Sections change at track 1's loop boundary, and the last section stops the song.
Take a jam
While you jam with no song playing, each loop of track 1 is logged as a section. Hold REC on SONG, or use Take jam on the sheet, to turn that into the arrangement.
OCT+ sheet
Insert, Duplicate or Delete a section, Take jam, or Clear song.
Drummer
A section with a groove starts the drummer on that groove from the section's first step. Your own drum pattern comes back when the song stops.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Make a few patterns first.
  2. Open SEQ > SONG and add sections in playback order.
  3. Choose each track's pattern and the repeats.
  4. Press PLAY to audition, then stop and save the project.
SynthMaven development source | Sequencer22

SEQUENCER

Saving a pattern

OPEN THIS SCREENStudio > Sequencer.
In the editors
On Studio > Sequencer, choose a pattern under Save to and tap Save pattern. Tap again to confirm, because it replaces what is in that pattern.
On the FM-1
Open SEQ > PATTERNS, press OCT+ for the sheet and choose Save to.
Then
The saved pattern can be loaded onto its track in the Arranger. Save a project to keep it.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Build the pattern in the step sequencer.
  2. Save it to one of the track's 8 patterns.
  3. Choose it in a section of the Arranger.

PERFORMANCE

Punch effects

OPEN THIS SCREENHold FX.
FX + key
Hold FX and press a key to apply one of 27 effects to the whole stereo master. Let go of the key for dry audio.
Double-tap FX
Lock the layer; tap again to close it.
Effects
Loops, reverse, tape stop, half speed, filter sweeps, phone, crush, alias, gate, echo, wobble, band kills, rewind, octave up, flanger, auto-pan, freeze, mono and fade.
KNOB 1
Browse the key reference.
Notes
Effect keys play no notes and send no MIDI. Keys already held keep playing.
Reverse and rewind
Hold FX briefly first, so there is audio history to play back.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Start a groove.
  2. Hold FX and press an effect key at the end of a phrase.
  3. Let go to return to the dry sound.

WEB AND IPAD EDITOR

Per-layer MIDI routing

Open
Settings > MIDI > Routing.
Where
In the editors: Settings > MIDI > Routing.
Layers and drummer
Assign an input (Any, USB or TRS) and a channel (Off, 1-16 or All) to layers 1-4 and the Drummer. Routing is off by default and is saved on the FM-1.
Splits and stacks
Layers on the same input and channel split or stack by note range.
Drummer
Plays and records on the first part using the DRUM engine; that part is then not available as a layer.
MIDI Learn
Adds Transport Play / Stop, Record (selected part) and Record (drummer).
STEP BY STEP
  1. Connect in COMPUTER role and open the editor.
  2. Turn routing on.
  3. Choose an input and channel for each layer and the Drummer.
  4. Play each keyboard and check it reaches the right layer.
SynthMaven development source | Web and iPad editor27

WEB AND IPAD EDITOR

Playing with several keyboards

Open
Settings > MIDI > Routing.
Two keyboards by input
Put one on TRS and one on USB. Route each layer to the input that should play it.
Several on one input
Give each keyboard its own channel, and route each layer to one channel.
Controllers through a computer
The web editor can forward several controllers on a computer, each to its target's channel.
Controllers through an iPad
The iPad app forwards one controller at a time.
Directly into the FM-1
Set USB ROLE to HOST and use a powered data hub. The FM-1 can't power a USB controller itself. HOST and the editors can't be used over USB at the same time.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Decide which keyboard plays which layers.
  2. Set each keyboard's MIDI channel on the keyboard.
  3. Set Routing to match.
  4. Save the program.
SynthMaven development source | Web and iPad editor28

WEB AND IPAD EDITOR

Maqam tuning workflow

Open
Tap SEL, or open the Tuning tab.
SEL (tap)
Master tuning. SELECT or KNOB 1 chooses the scale: a list of full names opens over the keyboard and closes itself when you stop turning. The tuning changes as you browse, and OCT- puts back the scale you started on. KNOB 2 the lower octave boundary, KNOB 3 the root, KNOB 4 turns it on. Arabic scales show as A/ on the panel.
SEL (hold three seconds)
Custom tuning. KNOB 1 chooses the key, KNOB 2 changes its offset in 10-cent steps, KNOB 3 quantizes all, KNOB 4 applies master tuning to the selected part.
Editors
Tap a key and use the wheel for 1-cent steps. Hold an untuned key for one second for -50 cents; hold an adjusted key to reset it.
Octave boundary
Notes below it stay in equal temperament, which keeps bass and chords usable.
Per part
Each part can bypass master tuning, so a piano layer can stay in equal temperament.
Programs
Tuning survives program changes unless a program includes its own tuning.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Tap SEL and choose a scale and root.
  2. Choose the octave boundary.
  3. Turn on master tuning.
  4. Bypass any part that should stay in equal temperament.
SynthMaven development source | Web and iPad editor29

WEB AND IPAD EDITOR

MainStage-style performance: programs, scenes and setlists

Open
Studio > Programs.
Program
Four parts with levels, pans, splits and scenes. P1-P8 are stored on the device.
Scene
Four per program: snapshots of levels, pans, mutes, effect sends, HYBRID macros and tuning.
Setlist
An ordered list of up to 32 references to P1-P8. A program can appear more than once.
Pedals and controllers
MIDI Learn assigns up to 16 actions, including Scene or Setlist Next / Previous.
Panel
On HOME, hold OCT- or OCT+ for three seconds for the previous or next program.
Editors
The Perform screen has program and scene navigation, a mixer and quick controls. Tuning has its own tab.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Build a program for each song and save it.
  2. Capture scenes in Programs & scenes, then save the program.
  3. Build the setlist.
  4. Learn a pedal to Scene Next and Setlist Next.

WEB AND IPAD EDITOR

Editor / MIDI routing for layers and the drummer

Open
Open the matching editor page shown below.
Controls and workflow
Open Settings → MIDI → Routing and turn on Use custom routing. While it is on, it replaces SYSTEM → ROUT.
Controls and workflow
For each of layers 1–4 and the Drummer, choose an input (Any, USB or TRS) and a channel (Off, 1–16 or All channels).
Controls and workflow
To split or stack, give two layers the same input and channel, then set their lowest and highest notes. Separate ranges split the keyboard; overlapping ranges stack. Note ranges are saved with the program.
Controls and workflow
Set one part to the DRUM engine for the Drummer. Pads play and record on that part, so it is not available as a layer. A layer cannot share an input and channel with the Drummer.
Controls and workflow
Choose Save to FM-1 between songs: saving releases held notes. Routing is saved on the device and applies in COMPUTER and HOST.
Controls and workflow
To record from a pedal, use Learn & actions: Transport Play / Stop, Record (selected part) and Record (drummer). One part records at a time.
Controls and workflow
On a computer, Connection & forwarding sends each connected controller to a target on that target's channel. Forwarding stops when the editor closes, and is not available in HOST, where one USB controller is served.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Connect the real FM-1 in COMPUTER USB role. Mock mode changes demonstration data only.
  2. Choose the part and screen before editing. Touch arrows cycle choices; card tabs reveal the remaining controls.
  3. Save the sound/program/project as appropriate; a browser library copy is separate.

WEB AND IPAD EDITOR

Editor / Four-layer melodic sequencer

Open
Studio > Sequencer > Steps.
Four lanes
Each visible lane belongs to the matching program layer. Tap a step to select its layer and edit that step. The selected lane and step have an outline.
Steps
Eight steps are visible at a time. Previous/next step arrows expose the remaining steps without changing the pattern.
Notes A0-C8
Choose from all 88 piano notes in each of four note selectors. Use the dash for an empty chord slot. Notes are selectable, not free text.
Length / Accent / Slide
NOTE triggers the selected pitches, TIE connects steps, REST leaves silence. Accent and slide retain the firmware behavior.
Velocity / Chance
Velocity sets note strength, from 0 to 127. Chance sets probability from 0 to 100 percent.
Pattern / Play / Save
Choose one of eight patterns for the selected layer. Play runs on the connected FM-1. Save the project to retain patterns and arrangement.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Select a layer and a pattern. Tap a step and choose one or more notes.
  2. Set note length, velocity, chance, accent and slide as needed; repeat for other layers.
  3. Open Studio > Arranger, arrange the patterns, then save the project. Use Drums for independent drum patterns.
SynthMaven development source | Web and iPad editor52

WEB AND IPAD EDITOR

Editor / Arranger

Open
Studio > Arranger.
Grid
Rows are the four layers plus Drums, and columns are the sections. Choose a saved pattern for each layer and a groove for Drums in each section, plus its repeats. Use Add section to extend the song.
Track 1-4 patterns
Each section selects one of eight patterns independently for each track. Side arrows cycle the pattern number; track colors identify the four parts.
Repeats
Play this section 1-16 times before moving to the next. A song contains up to 16 ordered sections.
Add / Copy / Move left / Delete
Add a section, duplicate a section, move it left or remove it. Structural edits are disabled while the song is playing.
Play from start / Stop
Play the arrangement on the connected FM-1. The current section and remaining repeats are reported by the device.
Projects & backup
Save the current project in A-D to retain the arrangement, then export a backup. Patterns must already contain melodic notes to produce sound; independent drums are edited on the Drums page.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Create patterns in Studio > Sequencer for each of the four tracks.
  2. Open Studio > Arranger; add sections and choose four patterns, a groove and repeats for each.
  3. Play from start, stop to edit, then use Projects & backup to save.

SAVE

PROGRAM

OPEN THIS SCREENTap SAVE; PROGRAM is the first page. Stop playback before writing a save.
KNOB 1 - SLOT
Choose saved program slot P1-P8. Values: 1 to 8.
KNOB 2 - NAME
Change the character at the current name position. ALGORITHM chooses the position; PRESET also changes the character. Values: 1 to 12.
KNOB 3 - LOAD
Load the complete four-part program in the selected slot. Turn right twice within 1.5 seconds; turn left to cancel the armed action. Values: -- / GO.
KNOB 4 - SAVE
Save the complete four-part program in the selected slot. Turn right twice within 1.5 seconds; turn left to cancel the armed action. Values: -- / GO.
BUTTONS AND NAVIGATION
SELECT (or KNOB 1) chooses P1-P8. ALGORITHM chooses name position; PRESET/KNOB 2 edits the character. KNOB 3 loads and KNOB 4 saves with two right turns. Repeated SAVE opens PRESETS, USER and PROJECT; HOME exits.
KEEP YOUR CHANGES
Save the containing four-part PROGRAM to retain the sound and mix. Save a PROJECT for pattern banks and arrangements; export a USB backup for safekeeping.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Open this screen using the path above; check the selected part or row before turning a knob.
  2. Change one setting at a time. Play a note or pattern and compare the result; inactive routes or muted parts may make a control inaudible.
  3. Use HOME to leave, then save the appropriate program/project if you want a named version.

SCL

OPEN THIS SCREENOn HOME select the part, then press SEL. Use SELECT or repeated family-button taps to find SCL.
KNOB 1

KNOBS 3-4
No direct row editing on this list screen.
ROOT
Root note of the selected scale. This transposes the scale relationship; it does not transpose every played note. C to B
SCL
Keyboard scale used by note quantization and scale-aware chords. 70 named choices; browse the on-screen list.
QNT
OFF leaves note selection chromatic; SNAP moves notes to the chosen scale; WHITE maps white-key playing into that scale. ALL modes apply the setting across all four parts and MIDI input. OFF / SNAP / WHITE / ALL / MPC
DEG
Scale degree assigned to pad 02 in MPC quantization mode; establishes the pad-bank layout. 1 to 12
TRN
Transpose this part by semitones; octave shifts are multiples of 12. -24 to +24 st

KNOB 1 - A4
Reference frequency of A4, in Hz. This is separate from the tuning-system octave boundary. Values: 400 to 480 Hz.
KNOB 2 - BUDGET
Shared synthesis allocation budget (8-32 points). All four parts compete for this total; raising it can increase CPU load and crackling. Values: 8 to 64 pts.

Clock source: INT uses the FM-1 tempo; USB or TRS follows incoming MIDI clock on that connection. Values: INT / USB / TRS.
KNOB 4 - TUNE
Global fine pitch offset in cents, added to A4 and scale tuning. Values: -50 to 50.

FX

FX

OPEN THIS SCREENOn HOME select the part, then press FX. Use SELECT or repeated family-button taps to find FX.
KNOB 1 - NOTE FX
Select note processing for the highlighted part-rack row: OFF, NOTE TAIL or NOTE ECHO. Values: OFF / NOTE TAIL / NOTE ECHO.
KNOB 2 - ROW
Choose one of the three effect rows or the shared/return row.
KNOB 3
No parameter on the ordinary part effect row.
KNOB 4 - AMOUNT
Set the selected row mix/send; NOTE TAIL uses release amount. On RETURN, set the shared wet return level.
BUTTONS AND NAVIGATION
HOME returns to the four-part display. SELECT navigates pages. The family button advances pages. PLAY starts/stops transport; REC arms the selected track. OCT- backs out and OCT+ confirms where an action or picker is offered.
KEEP YOUR CHANGES
Save the containing four-part PROGRAM to retain the sound and mix. Save a PROJECT for pattern banks and arrangements; export a USB backup for safekeeping.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Open this screen using the path above; check the selected part or row before turning a knob.
  2. Change one setting at a time. Play a note or pattern and compare the result; inactive routes or muted parts may make a control inaudible.
  3. Use HOME to leave, then save the appropriate program/project if you want a named version.

Dry/wet balance or shared effect output level, as identified by the page. Values: 0 to 100 %.
KNOB 2 - DRIVE
Drive into a saturation/filter stage. More drive can add harmonics and change level. Values: 0 to 100 %.
KNOB 3 - TONE
Tone or spectral balance of this sound/processor. Values: 30 to 16.0 kHz.
KNOB 4 - SHAPE
Waveform/timbre shaping or the amount of envelope/LFO shaping, according to this page. Values: SOFT / HARD / FOLD / FUZZ.
BUTTONS AND NAVIGATION
HOME returns to the four-part display. SELECT navigates pages. The family button advances pages. PLAY starts/stops transport; REC arms the selected track. OCT- backs out and OCT+ confirms where an action or picker is offered.

ENV

ENV

OPEN THIS SCREENOn HOME select the part, then press ENV. Use SELECT or repeated family-button taps to find ENV.
KNOB 1 - ATK
Attack time: how quickly the envelope rises after a note starts. Values: 1.0 to 10.0 s.
KNOB 2 - DEC
Decay time from the attack peak to the sustain level. Values: 1.0 to 10.0 s.
KNOB 3 - SUS
Sustain level while the key or gate remains held; this is a level, not a time. Values: 0 to 100 %.
KNOB 4 - REL
Release time after key-up; longer tails continue to consume voices. Values: 1.0 to 10.0 s.
BUTTONS AND NAVIGATION

LFO DEST

OPEN THIS SCREENOn HOME select the part, then press LFO. Use SELECT or repeated family-button taps to find LFO DEST.
KNOB 1 - PIT
Pitch or pitch modulation depth. In an envelope/LFO destination page this is an amount, not a tuning reference. Values: -100 to +98 %.

Amplitude modulation depth. Start with a small amount to avoid large level swings. Values: 0 to 100 %.

PMS
Pitch-modulation sensitivity of the native FM voice. 0 to 7

KNOB 3 - TONE

KNOB 4 - DECY
Drum-kit decay amount. Shorten it for tighter hits and fewer overlapping tails. Values: 0 to 100 %.

EDIT

FM6 / FM BEND

OPEN THIS SCREENOn HOME choose FM6, then EDIT. Use its section/page navigation to reach FM BEND.
KNOB 1
Edit the highlighted row.
KNOB 2
Move the row highlight; the list scrolls to reveal the remaining settings.
KNOBS 3-4
No direct row editing on this list screen.
BEND+
Maximum upward pitch-bend interval in semitones. 0 to 12 st
BEND-
Maximum downward pitch-bend interval in semitones. 0 to 12 st
STEP
Pitch-bend step size; stepped bends move in discrete pitch intervals. 0 to 12
DXVEL
DX7-style velocity normalization/response option. Changes how incoming velocity reaches the FM engine. OFF / ON
PORTA
Select the FM portamento behavior; TIME sets the transition duration. PEDAL / ON
TIME
Portamento transition time: higher values produce a slower glide between notes. PORTA and GLISS determine its behavior. 0 to 127
GLISS
Quantize portamento into discrete semitone steps instead of a continuous slide. OFF / ON
ENGIN
FM rendering model. This changes the native FM implementation/character rather than selecting a different part. MODRN / MARK I / OPL
WHEEL
Response range/depth for the wheel MIDI performance controller. 0 to 99
W.DST
Destination combination for this controller: pitch, amplitude and/or envelope bias, according to the displayed choice. - / P / A / PA / E / PE / AE / PAE
FOOT
Response range/depth for the foot MIDI performance controller. 0 to 99
F.DST
Destination combination for this controller: pitch, amplitude and/or envelope bias, according to the displayed choice. - / P / A / PA / E / PE / AE / PAE
BRTH
Breath controller modulation range; B.DST selects its destination. 0 to 99
B.DST
Destination combination for this controller: pitch, amplitude and/or envelope bias, according to the displayed choice. - / P / A / PA / E / PE / AE / PAE
AFTER
Response range/depth for the after MIDI performance controller. 0 to 99
A.DST
Destination combination for this controller: pitch, amplitude and/or envelope bias, according to the displayed choice. - / P / A / PA / E / PE / AE / PAE
BUTTONS AND NAVIGATION
KNOB 2 selects a row and KNOB 1 changes it. OCT+ opens a choice list when available; OCT- returns to HOME. SELECT/family button moves between screens. PLAY/REC retain transport/recording roles.

KNOB 2 - WAVE2
Select the oscillator or modulation waveform. Changing the shape changes its harmonic content or movement. Values: OFF / SAW / SQUARE / PULSE / NULL / DBL SINE / SAW-PULS / MULTISIN / PULSE2.
KNOB 3 - W.KEY
Keyboard scaling of the waveform envelope: changes its response across the keyboard. Values: 0 to 9.
KNOB 4 - A.KEY
Keyboard scaling of the amplitude envelope: changes envelope response across the keyboard. Values: 0 to 9.
BUTTONS AND NAVIGATION
HOME returns to the four-part display. SELECT navigates pages. The family button advances pages. PLAY starts/stops transport; REC arms the selected track. OCT- backs out and OCT+ confirms where an action or picker is offered. Native engine sections can be opened from the EDIT section map; PRESET navigates sections/pages rather than replacing the sound there.
KEEP YOUR CHANGES
Save the containing four-part PROGRAM to retain the sound and mix. Save a PROJECT for pattern banks and arrangements; export a USB backup for safekeeping.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Open this screen using the path above; check the selected part or row before turning a knob.
  2. Change one setting at a time. Play a note or pattern and compare the result; inactive routes or muted parts may make a control inaudible.
  3. Use HOME to leave, then save the appropriate program/project if you want a named version.

KNOB 4 - OSC2
Second oscillator setting/level. Use the engine description to distinguish oscillator type from mix. Values: 0 to 100 %.
BUTTONS AND NAVIGATION
HOME returns to the four-part display. SELECT navigates pages. The family button advances pages. PLAY starts/stops transport; REC arms the selected track. OCT- backs out and OCT+ confirms where an action or picker is offered. Native engine sections can be opened from the EDIT section map; PRESET navigates sections/pages rather than replacing the sound there.
KEEP YOUR CHANGES
Save the containing four-part PROGRAM to retain the sound and mix. Save a PROJECT for pattern banks and arrangements; export a USB backup for safekeeping.
STEP BY STEP
  1. Open this screen using the path above; check the selected part or row before turning a knob.
  2. Change one setting at a time. Play a note or pattern and compare the result; inactive routes or muted parts may make a control inaudible.
  3. Use HOME to leave, then save the appropriate program/project if you want a named version.

EDIT

VPS / EDIT 2

OPEN THIS SCREENOn HOME choose VPS, then EDIT. Use its section/page navigation to reach EDIT 2.
KNOB 1 - CUT
Low-pass/filter cutoff: lower values remove more upper harmonics. Values: 30 to 16.0 kHz.
KNOB 2 - RES
Filter resonance emphasizes frequencies around cutoff. High values may change level or approach self-oscillation. Values: 0 to 100 %.
KNOB 3 - DTN
Detuning amount between oscillators/voices or FM operators, according to the selected engine. Values: 0 to 100 %.
KNOB 4 - SUB
Sub-oscillator level under the main oscillator. Values: 0 to 100 %.

ARP

ARP

OPEN THIS SCREENOn HOME select the part, then press ARP. Use SELECT or repeated family-button taps to find ARP.
KNOB 1 - MODE
OFF, ascending, descending, up/down, random, played order or repeat patterns from held notes. Values: OFF / UP / DN / UPDN / RND / ORD / REPEAT.
KNOB 2 - RATE
Arpeggiator note division relative to tempo. T values are triplets. Values: 1/4 / 1/8 / 1/16 / 1/32 / 8T / 16T / 1/2 / 1/1 / 2BAR / 4BAR.
KNOB 3 - OCT
Number of octaves traversed by the arpeggiator. Values: 1 to 4.
KNOB 4 - GATE
Duration of each generated arp/sequence note as a fraction of its step. Values: 1 to 100 %.

ARP

ARP 2

OPEN THIS SCREENOn HOME select the part, then press ARP. Use SELECT or repeated family-button taps to find ARP 2.
KNOB 1 - SWG
Off-beat timing offset. Zero is straight; higher settings delay alternating subdivisions. Values: 0 to 100 %.
KNOB 2 - PROB
Probability of playing a generated note. Lower settings deliberately omit some notes. Values: 0 to 100 %.
KNOB 3 - HOLD
Keep the arpeggiated/held notes after key-up. Turn off to release the latched note set. Values: OFF / ON.
KNOB 4 - ORD
Order in which held notes enter the arpeggiator. Values: NOTE / PLAY.

SEQ

TEMPO

OPEN THIS SCREENOn HOME select the part, then press SEQ. Use SELECT or repeated family-button taps to find TEMPO.
KNOB 1 - BPM
Internal tempo in beats per minute. Values: 40 to 240 BPM.
KNOB 2 - SWG
Off-beat timing offset. Zero is straight; higher settings delay alternating subdivisions. Values: 0 to 100 %.
KNOB 3 - QNT
Recording grid for the next take on all tracks. OFF preserves timing; divisions snap recording to the grid. Does not rewrite an existing take. Values: OFF / 1/4 / 1/8 / 1/16 / 1/32 / 8T / 16T / 1/2 / 1/1 / 2BAR / 4BAR.
KNOB 4
No assigned parameter on this page.

SynthMaven development source Illustrated Guide

SynthMaven development source | EDIT hold286

EDIT HOLD

LAYER MIX

OPEN THIS SCREENHold EDIT for two seconds, then release. The mixer stays open until you leave it.
KNOB 1 - VOL1
Volume of part 1. This is independent of which part SELECT currently focuses. Values: 0 to 100 %.
KNOB 2 - VOL2
Volume of part 2. This is independent of which part SELECT currently focuses. Values: 0 to 100 %.
KNOB 3 - VOL3
Volume of part 3. This is independent of which part SELECT currently focuses. Values: 0 to 100 %.
KNOB 4 - VOL4
Volume of part 4. This is independent of which part SELECT currently focuses. Values: 0 to 100 %.
BUTTONS AND NAVIGATION
SELECT focuses part 1-4. PRESET pans the focused part. ALGORITHM sets its lower split point A1-A6. KNOBS 1-4 always control the four volumes. HOME exits; hold GLO for two seconds to toggle layering.
